---
title: "Figure 1.1.1: US Citizen Departures to the Caribbean"
---

![Python: `python/fig-1-1-1.py`](../images/python/fig-1-1-1.png)

Monthly departures for three years as bars side by side, with the
year-over-year change as a line on a right-hand scale.

**New in this chart:**

- grouped bars;
- a right-hand scale built directly with `twinx()`;
- a legend that combines bars from one axes object with a line from another.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 6 rows (January to June):

| category | 2019 | 2025 | 2026 | Year-over-year percent change (right scale) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 0.289 | 0.343 | 0.351 | 2.33 |

The column names are the years, as text. That is why the script uses the
strings `"2019"`, `"2025"` and `"2026"`.

## The script

```python
years = ["2019", "2025", "2026"]
year_colours = {"2019": "#0873B2", "2025": "#BFC0C2", "2026": "#A982BA"}
yoy = "Year-over-year percent change (right scale)"
```

The long column name of the line series is stored once in `yoy`, so it does
not have to be typed again.

### Grouped bars

```python
x = np.arange(len(data))
bar_width = 0.82 / len(years)
for i, year in enumerate(years):
    offset = (i - (len(years) - 1) / 2) * bar_width
    ax.bar(x + offset, data[year], width=bar_width, color=year_colours[year], label=year)
```

Each month is a category at position 0, 1, 2, .... The three bars of a month
together take 0.82 of the space between months, so each bar is 0.82 / 3
wide.

`enumerate(years)` numbers the years 0, 1, 2. The offset is then -1, 0 and
+1 bar widths, so the middle bar sits exactly on the month's position. See
[Grouped bars](../techniques.qmd#sec-grouped).

```python
ax.set_xticks(x, data["category"])
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(data) - 0.4)
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.8)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(0.2))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FormatStrFormatter("%.1f"))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=6)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=3, pad=6)
```

- **Number format.** `FormatStrFormatter("%.1f")` writes the y-labels with
  one decimal (0.0, 0.2, ...), as in the published chart. See [Number
  formats](../techniques.qmd#sec-number-formats).
- **No x-ticks.** `length=0` hides the x-axis ticks, as is usual for bar
  charts.

### The line on the right-hand scale

```python
ax_right = ax.twinx()
ax_right.plot(x, data[yoy], color="black", linewidth=1.8, solid_capstyle="round")
ax_right.set_ylim(0, 8)
ax_right.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(2))
ax_right.spines["right"].set_visible(True)
ax_right.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=3, pad=6)
```

This is what `add_right_axis()` from `chart_style` does, written out:

- **The twin.** `twinx()` creates a second plot area with the same x-axis and
  its own y-axis.
- **The right spine.** The house style hides the right spine, so it is
  switched back on.

The line is drawn on `ax_right`, so its values are read against the 0–8
scale. See [A right-hand scale](../techniques.qmd#sec-right-scale).

### One legend for both scales

```python
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
handles.append(Line2D([], [], color="black", linewidth=1.8))
labels.append(yoy)
ax_right.legend(
    handles, labels,
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.02),
    handlelength=3.2, handleheight=0.9, labelspacing=0.1,
    borderaxespad=0.2, fontsize=9.5,
)
```

`ax.get_legend_handles_labels()` returns what the legend of `ax` would show:
the three bar series with their labels. A sample line for the right-scale
series is added by hand (`Line2D([], [], ...)` is a line with no data, used
only as a legend symbol). The legend is placed on `ax_right`, which lies on
top, so the bars cannot cover it.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-1-1-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-1-1-1.py"}
"""Figure 1.1.1: US Citizen Departures to the Caribbean."""
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FormatStrFormatter, MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart

STEM = "fig-1-1-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

years = ["2019", "2025", "2026"]
year_colours = {"2019": "#0873B2", "2025": "#BFC0C2", "2026": "#A982BA"}
yoy = "Year-over-year percent change (right scale)"

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="US Citizen Departures to the Caribbean",
    subtitle="(Millions, unless noted otherwise)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: US International Trade Administration; and IMF staff\n"
        "calculations.\n"
        "Note: Data include 15 countries and exclude Jamaica."
    ),
    title_size=13.5,
    subtitle_size=11.5,
    caption_size=9,
    left=0.4,
    right=0.35,
    bottom_gap=0.3,
)

# Bars: one group per month, one bar per year.
x = np.arange(len(data))
bar_width = 0.82 / len(years)
for i, year in enumerate(years):
    offset = (i - (len(years) - 1) / 2) * bar_width
    ax.bar(x + offset, data[year], width=bar_width, color=year_colours[year], label=year)

ax.set_xticks(x, data["category"])
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(data) - 0.4)
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.8)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(0.2))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FormatStrFormatter("%.1f"))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=6)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=3, pad=6)

# Line: year-over-year change, on the right-hand scale.
ax_right = ax.twinx()
ax_right.plot(x, data[yoy], color="black", linewidth=1.8, solid_capstyle="round")
ax_right.set_ylim(0, 8)
ax_right.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(2))
ax_right.spines["right"].set_visible(True)
ax_right.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=3, pad=6)

handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
handles.append(Line2D([], [], color="black", linewidth=1.8))
labels.append(yoy)
ax_right.legend(
    handles, labels,
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.02),
    handlelength=3.2, handleheight=0.9, labelspacing=0.1,
    borderaxespad=0.2, fontsize=9.5,
)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
